evidence: Type allocation matches the ask. (1) Gates: task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:20 and gates/constraints/judge.toml:20 are type = "binary" with aggregation all_pass, as staged-task-contract.md:96 requires. (2) Functional: all 43 criteria in scored/functional/judge.toml are type = "binary" (e.g. :26 hro_job_open, :198 hro_stale_refused, :405 hro_restart); each is a discrete product rule with a stated 'Fails if...' bar (refusal/acceptance, ordering, permission, persistence, live arrival within 15 s), i.e. pass/fail behaviours; a grep for craft wording (clear|readable|quality|look|appropriate|reasonabl) finds only 'readable lines naming who and the stages' (:263) which is a presence test, not degree-of-quality. (3) Polish: all 5 criteria binary (hro_pol_live_board :20, hro_pol_live_thread :29, hro_pol_earlier_place :38, hro_pol_failed_send :47, hro_pol_session_resume :56); each grades an observable preservation behaviour (draft text equal, document.activeElement retained, scroll not reset, anchor message within a few px, failed send not lost/duplicated, re-auth prompt) - binary fits; the frozen template polish dimension is also all binary (template scored/polish/judge.toml:20,31,42,53). (4) Visual (craft): all 5 criteria type = "likert", points = 5 (scored/visual/judge.toml:20-21, 35-36, 50-51, 65-66, 80-81) and every one has a described anchor at each of levels 5,4,3,2,1 (e.g. :25-29 typography, :70-74 hierarchy). The visual prompt (scored/visual/prompt.md:7,12,16) consistently treats raw Likert 1 as the minimum ('normalizes to zero') and tells the judge to 'grade every criterion independently with its five anchors'. No binary craft criterion (lost gradation) and no likert block missing anchors exists, which is exactly what SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 tell this row to flag; per that known false positive, the internal E42 note ('Likert we dont use') is not a defect against the shipped likert visual dimension. Attempted counterexamples: a visually rough but functional app is graded on 1-5 gradations in Visual, not zeroed by a binary craft bar; a polished but rule-breaking app cannot buy functional/polish credit because those are behaviour binaries - no type misfit found. Risk reason (P3, non-blocking): anchor range differs from the frozen template, which supplies six anchors 0-5 for points = 5 (template scored/visual/judge.toml:25-33), while the task supplies 1-5 and asserts raw 1 normalizes to 0. rewardkit is not installed locally and raw-evidence-index.json states no configured judge run exists, so the actual likert range/normalization for points = 5 (1..5 vs 0..5) is unmeasured; if rewardkit treats 0 as a valid level, the task's lowest described anchor would not reach normalized 0. This is a missing-measurement gap, not a demonstrated defect in type fit.
